title: fix(plugin-hono-server): a Hono door's 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE carries currentVersion and currentRecord (#23531)
body:
Fixes #23531
Clause-②: no

## What this does

A stale `If-Match` on `PATCH` or `DELETE /data/:object/:id` is refused by the protocol with `ConcurrentUpdateError` (`409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE`). `RestServer` answers it with the server's `currentVersion` and `currentRecord`. Both Hono doors answered it with `code` and `message` only: `@objectstack/hono`'s `createHonoApp` (its `dispatch()` catch-all, through `thrownJson`) and a route mounted on `HonoHttpServer` (`wrap()`, and the transport `onError` seam). All three paths render through one function, `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` in `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`. That function forwarded only the `details` that the thrown-error resolver derives, and it never reads the two fields, because they are own properties of the error.

`declaredEnvelopeForThrow` now asks one helper beside it, `declaredConflictContext`. For a `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE`, that helper reads the conflict's context off `structuredCodeAnswer` (`@objectstack/types`, already exported). That is the arm `RestServer`'s `mapDataError` answers this conflict through. Everything the arm's body carries is forwarded except its own sentence and code, which the envelope already carries as `message` and `code`. So:

- ⛔ no third spelling of the conflict body: the fields are not listed in the Hono package. Each one appears only when the producer stated it, by the REST arm's own rule.
- the arm must agree with the envelope already decided (same status, same code), so it can only add context and never changes the answer;
- only `CONCURRENT_UPDATE` is taken, per the card's scope ruling. Other structured arms are listed under Acceptance notes.

**Where the fields land:** `error.details`. On the wrapped envelope (`{ success, error }`) that is the declared context slot (`ApiErrorSchema.details`), and it is where `@objectstack/client` reads a wrapped body's context (`error.details = errorBody.details ?? errorBody.error.details ?? errorBody`). That is what objectui's `normaliseClientError` reads `currentVersion` / `currentRecord` from. The REST door's flat body has no envelope, so it carries them at the top level.

- FROM (measured on this branch's pins before the fix): `409 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"CONCURRENT_UPDATE","message":"Record task/ID was modified by another user (current version T1, expected T0)"}}`
- TO: the same, plus `"details":{"currentVersion":"T1","currentRecord":{…the row…}}`

Status, `code` and `message` do not move. A throw that is not a `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE` renders byte-identically to before.

**Both doors pick the change up from `adapter.ts` alone:** `createHonoApp`'s `thrownJson` (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts`, not edited here; seat 1's #23532 holds it), `wrap()` through `runHandler`, the `onError` seam, and the metrics observer's status read all call `declaredEnvelopeForThrow`.

## ⚠️ Disclosure, stated before review rather than after

`currentRecord` is forwarded as the protocol threw it, exactly as `RestServer` forwards it, per the dispatch ruling ("Match `RestServer` exactly … a finding against both doors, not a reason to differ"). Read on `origin/main` `7ffc57846a`: the protocol reads that row with `probeRecord`, which is `engine.findOne(object, { where: { id }, context: { isSystem: true } })` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `probeRecord`). The OCC comparison runs before `engine.update` / `engine.delete` apply the caller's write policy, and no layer narrows the row. So a caller who sends a stale `If-Match` for a row, or for fields of it, that they cannot read would get the system-context row back in the `409`. That has always been true at the REST door. This PR extends the same answer to the two Hono doors. It was not measured at a door with a security plugin booted. It is reported to the seat as a disclosure finding against the producer, and it covers both doors. The reviewer should weigh it before landing.

## Tests

The pins, the ablation and the package runs below were taken at `d7484b8621`. `origin/main` was then merged in (`9d467b933a`). That merge brought seat 1's `thrownJson` fallback-arm change from #23532, and it touched neither `plugin-hono-server` nor `@objectstack/types`. On the merged head `9d467b933a`, `metadata-protocol` was rebuilt and these were re-run: `@objectstack/http-conformance` `vitest run` (`Test Files 13 passed`, `Tests 139 passed`), and the direct-mount file (`Tests 23 passed (23)`).

- **New pins, red before the fix** (built tree at `13b5267b42`, tests only):
  - `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/handler-throw-declared-envelope.test.ts`, the `[#23531]` block: a direct-mount `PATCH` and `DELETE` route that judges `If-Match` and throws a `ConcurrentUpdateError`-shaped refusal. `× PATCH …`, `× DELETE …`: `expected undefined to deeply equal { …(2) }`; `Tests 2 failed | 21 passed (23)`.
  - `packages/qa/http-conformance/src/hono-declared-envelope.conformance.test.ts`, the `[#23531]` block: a real `createHonoApp` over the real dispatcher and protocol (SQLite WASM), stale `If-Match` `PATCH` and `DELETE`. The body read was `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"CONCURRENT_UPDATE","message":"Record task/… was modified by another user (current version 2026-10-15T00:47:11.377Z, expected 2001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z)"}}`, then `expected undefined to match object`; `Tests 2 failed | 13 passed (15)`.
  - `currentVersion` is proved by use, not by spelling: echoed as the next `If-Match`, it is accepted (`PATCH` writes, `DELETE` deletes).
  - Two controls pass on both trees: the version the route stores is accepted, and a conflict that states no current state keeps the two-key envelope.
- **Green after:** `plugin-hono-server` `Tests 23 passed (23)`; conformance `Tests 15 passed (15)`.
- **Ablation** (`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, wrap mode, plus an outer `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore against the absolute path):
  - anchor ``if (resolved.code !== 'CONCURRENT_UPDATE') return undefined;`` was replaced by the same line comparing to `ABLATION_23531_NO_SUCH_CODE` (anchor x1 to x0, replacement x0 to x1, blob `8e0d9721b86b` to `c4ebfc79a791`);
  - `plugin-hono-server` rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` reported the marker present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.mjs`;
  - the four field pins went RED, the predicted direction (unit `2 failed | 21 passed`, conformance `2 failed | 13 passed`);
  - restore: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty; rebuilt; preflight `--absent` showed the marker gone from all 6 built files with a clean tree; both suites green again.
- **Packages:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server typecheck` (tsc, `tsconfig.typecheck.json`, `check:test-typecheck` OK with 0 debt) and `test` (`Test Files 29 passed`, `Tests 340 passed`); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance typecheck` (`check:test-typecheck` OK, ledger unchanged) and `vitest run` (`Test Files 13 passed`, `Tests 139 passed`).
- `@objectstack/hono`'s own suite is not run locally: its vitest config stubs `@objectstack/runtime`, its source is untouched, and the composed-host pin above covers its behaviour. It is declared to CI.

## Changeset

`.changeset/23531-hono-conflict-body.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` `patch` and `@objectstack/hono` `patch`, with FROM → TO. `@objectstack/hono` is named because `createHonoApp`'s answer is the measured door, and its CHANGELOG carries the #23365 entry that states this gap. Nothing in its own files changes, and both packages are in the one fixed version group, so naming it moves no version.

## Acceptance notes

- **Same family, measured, not fixed here (scope ruling):** the other structured arms of the same classification are dropped by the Hono doors the same way. Measured at `d7484b8621` through a real `createHonoApp` (scratch test, not committed): `DELETE /data/parent/ID` of a row a `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'` lookup references answered `409 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"DELETE_RESTRICTED","message":"This Parent is still referenced by 1 Child record(s) through “Parent”. Delete or reassign them first."}}`. That body has no `developerMessage`, `dependentObject`, `dependentCount` or `object`, all of which `RestServer`'s arm carries. Not measured: `METADATA_CONFLICT`'s `currentVersion`, and the engine's `INVALID_FIELD`. Reported to the seat for the family's closing card. Widening `declaredConflictContext` from one code to "the arm agrees on status and code" is the mechanical shape.
- `object` is not forwarded: `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` has no route context, so the arm is asked without one, and the arm adds `object` only when given one.
- The adapter-side file surface is `declaredEnvelopeForThrow`, the helper beside it, and one added name on the existing `@objectstack/types` import. No new export.
